title: Asking what several things are
summary: Build the bounded plural classification question Mitä nämä ovat? and its nuo and ne counterparts.
objectives: Begin the bounded plural classification question with mitä.
Use a supplied plural demonstrative phrase.

sections.title: See the pattern
paragraphs: Use Mitä ... ovat? for the bounded beginner question asking what several things are.
The plural demonstrative phrase stands between mitä and ovat.

sections.title: Use one clear decision
paragraphs: This lesson treats mitä as part of this specific frame rather than teaching the general partitive system.
Mitkä meaning “which ones” is deliberately deferred.

steps: Mitä: the bounded plural classification form.
nämä rakennukset: the complete phrase is supplied.
Mitä: the bounded plural classification form.
nuo rakennukset: the complete phrase is supplied.
Mitä: the bounded plural classification form.
ne rakennukset: the complete phrase is supplied.

commonMistakes: Do not replace mitä with mikä in this plural frame.
Do not use on with the plural subject.
Do not introduce mitkä as an accepted equivalent in this bounded lesson.

practiceExercises.explanation: Mitä ... ovat asks what several things are. In English, begin with “What are” before the subject.

optionFeedback.Mitä nuo paikat ovat?: Correct. The bounded plural classification frame begins with Mitä and ends with ovat.
optionFeedback.Mikä nuo paikat ovat?: “Mikä” is the singular identity-question word used in this bounded frame; use “Mitä”, the plural classification-question word used in this bounded frame.
optionFeedback.Nuo paikat ovat?: “Nuo” is a plural nominative form for farther, jointly visible referents; use “Mitä”, the plural classification-question word used in this bounded frame.
optionFeedback.Mitä nuo paikat on?: “on” is the singular affirmative form of olla; use “ovat”, the plural affirmative form of olla.
